chunks: From what al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman and Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn 'Udhafir, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about Salat al-Layl and al-Witr after the rise of dawn. He said: Pray it after dawn, so long as it remains within a time in which you would pray the morning prayer at the end of its time, and do not intentionally do that every night. And he said: Perform the Witr also after you finish it.

key_terms.آخِرِ وَقْتِهَا: the end of its prescribed time
key_terms.الْغَدَاةَ: the morning prayer, meaning Salat al-Fajr
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: dawn; here referring to the onset of the morning prayer time
key_terms.الْوِتْرِ: the single-unit concluding prayer of the night prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed in the late night hours
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: the rising of dawn marking the beginning of the Fajr time
key_terms.فَرَاغِكَ: your completion or finishing of the preceding prayer

ai.seo_question: Can Salat al-Layl and Witr be prayed after Fajr has risen?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing Salat al-Layl and al-Witr after the rise of dawn. It indicates permissibility within a limited time connected to the end of the time of the morning prayer, while discouraging making this delay a regular habit.
